One-line verdict: cleaning, washing and metal pickling equipment operators are not about throwing things into a machine; they operate and tend cleaning and pickling equipment to process specifications, mix and replenish chemical agents, monitor temperature and concentration and cycle time, check the equipment and the cleaning result, and are accountable for solution condition and the production log; O*NET defines the occupation as operating or tending machines that wash products (such as barrels and glassware and tin plate and food and pulp and coal and plastics or rubber) to remove impurities.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to repeat work to procedure in noisy conditions with chemicals and high temperatures, you wear protective equipment as required, and you judge and record from instrument readings; the O*NET Work Context fields show that 100% wear common protective or safety equipment every day, 70% stand continuously or almost continuously, 70% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day, 41% are exposed to contaminants every day, 39% work indoors in a non-environmentally controlled setting every day, and 72% work a typical 40-hour week.

Conditions that warrant pausing before heavy investment: you have not yet run a full cleaning or pickling cycle to the process card, nor checked the mix ratios, concentrations and safety requirements of the chemical agents; this occupation's job zone is Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation), the SVP range is below 6.0, and the occupation page gives no percentages for the education distribution, listing only three post requirements (some posts require high school or equivalent, some require below high school, some require some college but no degree). Opportunities depend more on working to procedure and safety awareness, but safety responsibility for corrosive chemicals, high temperatures, rotating equipment and sealed tanks cannot be skipped, and the occupation page lists no national certification.

Education, qualifications and authority must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation) with an SVP range below 6.0; in cleaning and pickling work, being hired for a post, an employer's internal process training and operating authorisation, the statutory requirements for hazardous chemicals and pressure vessels and special operations, and authority to set process parameters and sign off releases are four different things; the O*NET occupation page lists no national certification, and this page does not present any training as a prerequisite for hiring or authorisation.

In one line: this is an occupation where reading parameters accurately, holding solution and equipment condition, and stopping and reporting anomalies in time matter more to success than working fast; if you are willing to repeat work to process specifications and take responsibility for the safety of the chemicals and equipment you handle, it is worth serious consideration.

Cleaning, washing and metal pickling equipment operator work falls into three connected but independent work surfaces. The first is solution and parameter management: adding specified amounts of chemical agents to the equipment at set times to maintain solution level and concentration as the process requires, measuring and weighing or mixing cleaning solutions with measuring tanks and calibrated rods or pipettes, and emptying and cleaning and refilling machines or tanks at designed intervals. The second is equipment operation and monitoring: setting controls to regulate temperature and cycle duration and starting conveyors and pumps and agitators and machines, watching the machine run and the instruments or thermometers and adjusting the controls as needed to hold the specified conditions, checking and patrolling the machines to find faults in time, and adjusting and cleaning and lubricating mechanical parts with tools and grease guns. The third is sampling and recording and loading and unloading: drawing samples for laboratory analysis or testing the solution against specification on site (such as acidity or specific gravity), operating or tending machines that wash barrels and glassware and tin plate surfaces and dried fruit and pulp and coal and finished goods and plastics or rubber and similar objects, loading objects into the machine and unloading them after washing and placing them on conveyors or racks, and entering instrument readings and materials used and processing times and test results in the production log. This is a description of occupational tasks, not a procedure for dosing, tank entry or maintenance; each stage must be carried out within the limits of actual training and authorisation.
Operate or tend cleaning and pickling equipment to remove impurities

Confirm the products to be cleaned and the process requirements → mix and replenish chemical agents and check the concentration → set the temperature and cycle duration and start the conveyor and pumps and agitator → watch the instruments and equipment and adjust as needed → empty, clean and top up the tank solution and take samples for testing → record readings, materials used and processing times and hand over
Maintain the solution and equipment condition to procedure and leave a production record

Check the production task and the product list → dose to the formula and measure and mix the solution → set and monitor the temperature and cycle time → load and unload products and place the washed items on the conveyor or rack → inspect the equipment and the cleaning result and handle anomalies → complete the production log and hand over the shift

Production log and instrument reading records, dosing and mix-ratio and solution test records, equipment inspection and lubrication and maintenance records, sampling and laboratory submission records, loading and unloading and output records; in some organisations also shutdown and leak and anomaly-handling records.

Common adjacent roles include food and tobacco roasting and drying equipment operators and tenders, food cooking equipment operators and tenders, metal and plastic grinding, polishing and buffing machine operators and tenders, metal smelting furnace operators and tenders, and metal and plastic heat treating equipment operators and tenders and cooling and freezing equipment operators and tenders. On the boundaries: the cleaning and pickling direction centres on solution and chemical and tank-liquid management; the food direction handles food ingredients and hygiene requirements; the grinding and polishing direction removes surface material and controls dimensions; the smelting and heat treating directions control the structure and properties of metals; the cooling and freezing direction controls temperature and the cold chain; this occupation cleans objects to remove impurities and maintains solution concentration.
Operate equipment within the process specification and operating procedures and maintain the solution and equipment condition

Food roasting, drying or cooking centres on the corresponding processing steps; this occupation centres on machine washing or removing impurities, and the O*NET object list also includes food, dried fruit and pulp, so whether something is food cannot be used to divide the occupations.

Based on the process card, the solution specification and the equipment manual; on O*NET the leading work activities are inspecting equipment and materials, documenting information, communicating with supervisors and co-workers, obtaining information and monitoring processes and materials

Food cooking equipment operators and tenders operate cooking and sterilising equipment to process food; this occupation operates cleaning and pickling equipment and manages chemical agents and tank liquids

Receive the production task, check the products and process, mix and replenish solutions, set and monitor parameters, load and unload products, inspect the equipment and the cleaning result, record and hand over

Editorial comparison: grinding and polishing focus on abrasives, dimensions and finish; this occupation centres on machine washing and removing impurities, without asserting that no cleaning process has any dimensional or surface-quality limits.

Production log and solution test records, dosing and mix-ratio records, equipment inspection and maintenance records, sampling and laboratory submission records, loading and unloading and output records

Smelting centres on treating metal in the furnace and heat treating centres on the heating and cooling process; this occupation mainly uses equipment to clean and remove impurities, so the process purpose differs. The absolute boundary that pickling never changes metal composition or structure is not asserted.

Six recurring occupational judgements: whether the process requirements and the product list are clearly confirmed; whether the agent mix ratios and solution concentration are properly checked; whether temperature and cycle time are set to specification and monitored; whether the solution and equipment condition is checked and maintained on schedule; whether sampling and testing and anomalies are handled as required; and whether the process data leaves a traceable record.
Judgement one: are the process requirements and the product list clearly confirmed

First confirm this batch's products, the cleaning or pickling specification and the permitted handling, and check the materials for which it is not suitable; when in doubt, ask before feeding the line.
Judgement two: are the agent mix ratios and solution concentration properly checked

Check the agents and specified amounts against the actual process documents, labels and safety data sheets; measuring, mixing, sampling and concentration testing are each carried out under the corresponding training and methods, and measuring tanks, calibrated rods or pipettes are not treated directly as a universal concentration test method.
Judgement three: are temperature and cycle time set to specification and monitored

Set the temperature and cycle duration from the process card and start the equipment, keep watching the instruments or thermometers and adjust as needed; do not extend or shorten the cycle on your own.
Judgement four: is the solution and equipment condition checked and maintained on schedule

O*NET has tasks for inspecting equipment and adjusting, cleaning and lubricating mechanical parts; actual maintenance must be carried out by trained and authorised personnel under the equipment energy control procedure, and an ordinary shutdown or power-off does not automatically prove that stored energy has been eliminated.
Judgement five: are sampling and testing and anomalies handled as required

Editorial anomaly note: on finding a leak or equipment anomaly, stop the affected work under the plan, protect personnel and report; isolation, depressurising and handling are carried out by trained and authorised personnel, and untrained people do not approach the fault. Resumption must meet the actual approval and safety conditions.
Judgement six: does the process data leave a traceable record
Write instrument readings, materials used, processing times and test results into the production log so that quality tracing and handover can be tied to a specific batch and operator.

Cleaning, washing and metal pickling equipment operators operate or tend machines that wash products such as barrels and glassware and tin plate and food and pulp and coal and plastics or rubber to remove impurities; the typical closed loop is confirming the products and process requirements, mixing and replenishing chemical agents and maintaining concentration, setting and monitoring temperature and cycle time, loading and unloading products and checking the equipment and cleaning result, sampling and testing and handling anomalies to procedure, and leaving a traceable production log.

O*NET51-9192.00, updated 2026, operates or tends equipment that washes products and removes impurities; interest RC, Job Zone1—2, SVP below 6. The certification search currently returns no entries, which does not prove that no certification exists; typical education and training values are checked separately against the exact BLS item.

Time and pace | 72% work a typical 40-hour week; 46% consider repeating the same task very important; 48% consider the pace being determined by equipment speed very important; 34% consider precision or accuracy quite important. Environment and exposure | 100% wear common protective or safety equipment every day; 70% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day; 41% are exposed to contaminants every day; 39% are indoors in a non-environmentally controlled setting every day; 25% are never in an environmentally controlled indoor setting; 31% are never exposed to extremely hot or cold temperatures. Posture and movement | 70% stand continuously or almost continuously; 34% bend or twist about half the time; 28% make repetitive motions less than half the time; 25% handle or feel objects and tools about half the time. Equipment and pace | The running cycle of the cleaning and pickling equipment sets the work pace; continuous monitoring of instruments and temperature and concentration is needed. Nature of the work | Mainly operating and tending cleaning and pickling equipment and mixing solutions and recording the production log; output must meet the process specification and be traceable. Safety and authority | Work involving corrosive chemicals, high temperatures, rotating equipment and sealed tanks must follow operating procedures and be carried out under authority; on finding a leak or equipment anomaly, shut down and isolate and report. paragraphs: The six directions share part of their skills with this occupation: operating equipment to process parameters, watching instruments and adjusting as needed, checking and maintaining equipment, recording process data, and following safety and protection requirements. The real differences lie in the objects handled and the process media (food ingredients, finished food, metal and plastic surfaces, molten metal, structure and properties, low-temperature environments) and the professional judgement required (hygiene requirements, dimensional accuracy, composition control, structure control, cold chain). When choosing, it is better to first validate with one deliverable parameter monitoring and recording exercise than to compare names.

The comparison is based on the task and work activity descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 51-9192.00 page, the adjacent-occupation notes registered by this evidence route, and public occupational material for each adjacent occupation; the comparison is an editorial arrangement and does not constitute a conclusion about practice scope or interchangeable qualifications.

The table below compares roles and occupations adjacent to this one: food and tobacco roasting and drying equipment operators and tenders, food cooking equipment operators and tenders, metal and plastic grinding, polishing and buffing machine operators and tenders, metal smelting furnace operators and tenders, and metal and plastic heat treating equipment operators and tenders and cooling and freezing equipment operators and tenders. The four columns answer the same kind of question: what this direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choosing it.

Food and tobacco roasting and drying equipment operators and tenders control roasting and drying curves to process food and tobacco ingredients; this occupation handles objects such as barrels and glassware and tin plate and plastics or rubber and manages cleaning and pickling solutions.

People willing to control temperature and time to a curve when processing food ingredients suit that direction; people willing to manage solutions and agents and clean various objects suit this occupation.
Mainly the roasted and dried food and tobacco products and the process records.
Food and tobacco roasting and drying equipment operators and tenders

Food cooking equipment operators and tenders operate cooking and sterilising equipment to process food and follow food hygiene requirements; this occupation operates cleaning and pickling equipment and manages agents and tank liquids, so the media and hygiene requirements differ.
People willing to do food cooking and sterilising and accept hygiene rules suit that direction; people willing to do industrial cleaning and pickling and agent management suit this occupation.
Mainly the cooked and sterilised food products and the hygiene and process records.
Food cooking equipment operators and tenders

Metal and plastic grinding, polishing and buffing machine operators and tenders use abrasives to remove surface material and control dimensions and finish; this occupation uses cleaning and agents to remove impurities and does no dimensional machining.
People willing to do grinding and polishing and control dimensional accuracy suit that direction; people willing to manage solutions and cleaning processes suit this occupation.
Mainly the machined dimensions and finish and the inspection records.
Metal and plastic grinding, polishing and buffing machine operators and tenders

Metal smelting furnace operators and tenders control the melting and refining process and metal composition; this occupation only handles the cleaning and pickling stage and does not change metal composition or structure.
People willing to control furnace temperature and the melting process suit that direction; people willing to do surface cleaning and solution management suit this occupation.
Mainly melting batches and composition testing and output records.
Metal smelting furnace operators and tenders

Metal and plastic heat treating equipment operators and tenders control the structure and properties of metals and plastics through heating and cooling; this occupation removes impurities by cleaning and does not carry process responsibility for structure and property control.
People willing to control heat treating curves and structure and properties suit that direction; people willing to do cleaning and pickling and solution management suit this occupation.
Mainly heat treating batches and hardness and structure testing records.
Metal and plastic heat treating equipment operators and tenders

Cooling and freezing equipment operators and tenders control refrigeration and freezing processes and maintain cold-chain temperatures; this occupation controls the temperature and concentration of cleaning and pickling tank liquids, so the objectives and media differ.
People willing to control refrigeration equipment and cold-store temperatures suit that direction; people willing to manage chemical solutions and cleaning processes suit this occupation.
Mainly the temperature and running records of cold stores and frozen products.
Cooling and freezing equipment operators and tenders

Moving from this occupation to an adjacent direction usually means adding new processes and qualifications: the food direction needs food hygiene and sterilising process knowledge, the grinding and polishing direction needs dimensional and abrasive and finish control capability, the smelting and heat treating directions need metallurgical and heat treating processes and the corresponding qualifications, and the cooling and freezing direction needs refrigeration equipment and cold-chain management training. Equipment operation and parameter monitoring and recording skills transfer, but each direction's process specifications and authorisation system must be obtained afresh.

values: Fictional task: using a fictional process card and the specification of a fictional cleaning and pickling machine, produce a plan for dosing and parameter setting and job records and write the anomaly handling.

Fictional materials: a fictional process card (including the tank-liquid concentration range and the temperature and cycle duration ranges), a fictional chemical label (including mix ratio and compatibility limits and protection requirements) and a fictional equipment manual extract (including the parameter upper limits that must not be exceeded).
Fictional condition: a fictional crew schedule (including the batch order and the handover deadline).
Fictional constraint: a fictional chemicals and confined-space management requirement (including protective equipment and waste-liquid disposal and entry permits and anomaly reporting).
Step one: write the dosing and mix-ratio plan (agent types and amounts and top-up water and concentration targets and measurement methods) and list the protective equipment needed.

Step two: from the process card, write the parameter setting and monitoring plan (temperature and cycle duration and sampling interval), and point out the two places most likely to go wrong (such as agent compatibility or over-temperature or over-pressure) and the corresponding checking method.

Step three: write the anomaly-handling and recording template (the conditions for shutdown and isolation and reporting and resuming work), and state which matters exceed your operating authority and must be referred to the team leader or a safety post.
Reference deliverables: one dosing and mix-ratio plan, one parameter setting and monitoring plan, and one anomaly-handling and recording template.

Assessment basis: whether the mix ratio and concentration are verifiable, whether parameters are within the equipment's permitted range, whether protection and compatibility are stated, whether the anomaly handling includes shutdown and reporting and resumption conditions, and whether matters inside and outside your authority are distinguished.
Several reasonable formulations are allowed; if you consider some information insufficient to judge, state clearly which parts are insufficient and what additional information is needed.

All materials in this exercise are fictional and must not be used for work on a real production line or tank; real work must be carried out by personnel with the appropriate authority and qualifications under the process documents, the operating procedures and local requirements.
The process parameters and chemical mix ratios given in the prompt are fictional values, to be used only to practise process planning and safety judgement methods.

entries.answer: Day-to-day work centres on solution and agent management, equipment operation and monitoring, and sampling and recording and loading and unloading: dosing to the process requirement and maintaining level and concentration, setting temperature and cycle duration and starting the conveyor and pumps and agitator, watching the instruments and adjusting as needed, emptying and cleaning and topping up the tank solution at designed intervals, inspecting and lubricating the equipment, sampling and testing whether the solution meets specification, and entering instrument readings and materials used and processing times in the production log. The O*NET Work Context fields show that 100% wear common protective or safety equipment every day, 70% stand continuously or almost continuously, 70% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day, and 72% work a typical 40-hour week.
entries.question: What do cleaning, washing and metal pickling equipment operators do every day?

entries.answer: The food and tobacco direction controls roasting and drying curves; the food cooking direction operates cooking and sterilising equipment; the grinding and polishing direction removes surface material and controls dimensions and finish; the smelting and heat treating directions control the composition and structure and properties of metals; the cooling and freezing direction maintains cold-chain temperatures; this occupation cleans objects to remove impurities and manages solution concentration. Shared skills do not mean the roles are interchangeable: the objects handled, the process media and the safety responsibility differ.

description.text: Cleaning, washing and metal pickling equipment operators operate and tend cleaning and pickling equipment to remove impurities, centring on equipment operation and monitoring, solution and agent management, and sampling and recording: tasks and work context, the US wage and employment basis shown on the O*NET page, the mainland China statistical gap, the entry and qualification pathway, risks and exercises, all in one view.

title.text: Cleaning, washing and metal pickling equipment operators

subject.name: Cleaning, washing and metal pickling equipment operators
subject.summary: Operate or tend machines that wash products such as barrels and glassware and tin plate and food and pulp and coal and plastics or rubber to remove impurities: dose to the process requirement and maintain level and concentration, set temperature and cycle duration and start the conveyor and pumps and agitator, watch the instruments and adjust as needed, empty and clean and top up the tank solution and take samples for testing, and load and unload products and enter the process data in the production log.
